_about: Maps. Walk off an edge listed in `exits` to travel to that map. `theme` picks ground tiles, ponds, fairy rings and scenery (art ids from art/assets.json); props with `cluster` grow in groups, `sway` ones move in the breeze. `ambience` adds particles (petals | leaves | fireflies | sparkles | bubbles | dandelions | sprinkles | lanterns | zzz | notes, joined with +), butterflies, `critters` that hop off when you come near (bunny | frog | crab), `birds` crossing the sky (songbirds | gulls | bats), cloud shadows, a colour tint and `weather` weights (clear | cloudy | rain | storm | fog | snow; {} for no sky). A prop with `bob` floats gently up and down. Maps with `encounters` have random battles; `music` is a song id from music.json. Building/decor/NPC x,y are tile offsets from the map centre (y up). Boss NPCs name their `monster` and `level`, `minions` (how many of the map's own monsters fight beside it, 9 unless set), `waves` (how many waves the fight comes in, 3 unless set: waves of 10 of the map's monsters, then the boss) and a `victory` story (a title and 1 to 3 short paragraphs), told the first time you beat it. `locals` are the people who live there (MapDef.Local in Content.swift): a name, a look, a home (`at` a landmark: jetty | bridge | island | shore | mouth, else on a `summit` or `x`, `y` out from the middle), `roam` or a `walk` there and back, maybe a `pet`, something to `hold`, armour to `wear` and `props` round them, and `lines`: their story, told a line at a time in order.

villagerLines: Mind the jellies past the gate.
The fountain sparkles at night, you know.
Have you visited the guilds yet?

locals.name: Little Lou
lines: I'm going to be an adventurer when I grow up!
Elder Oak says I need a sword. I've got a stick. Same thing.
Tess's brother went off adventuring. He isn't back yet.
When I'm big I'll go and find him. Unless you find him first!

npcs.name: Nurse Mira
npcs.greeting: Tired, dear? Rest here and your whole party will feel brand new.

npcs.name: Trader Bo
npcs.greeting: Potions, blades, robes — take a look!

npcs.name: Elder Oak
npcs.greeting: Ah, a new face! Meadowbrook could use a helping hand.

npcs.name: Captain Brann
npcs.greeting: The Warrior Guild wants strong arms and brave hearts.

npcs.name: Sage Lumi
npcs.greeting: The Arcane Circle studies the seven elements. Magic is a path of patience.

npcs.name: Ranger Pip
npcs.greeting: The Wildfolk Lodge! We befriend beasts, not beat them. Well, mostly.

npcs.name: Smith Tobin
npcs.greeting: Clang! Bring me wood and metal from the wilds and I'll forge you something fine.

locals.name: Old Fisher Gil
lines: Shh... they're biting today.
I've fished this lake since I was knee-high to a jelly.
Caught one THIS big once. Well... this big. Fine, a tadpole.
Come back at sunset. The whole lake turns gold.

locals.name: Tess
lines: My brother Wil crossed this bridge to see the world.
He said he'd be back before the blossoms fell.
The blossoms have fallen twice now.
He went east, to the dark woods. He's scared of the dark, you know.
If you meet a boy with a wooden sword, tell him Tess is waiting.

locals.name: Farmer Hollis
lines: Jelly Puffs ate my cabbages again!
I put up a scarecrow. They bounced on it.
Elder Oak says an adventurer will sort them out.
Is that you? You look like an adventurer. Mostly.

npcs.name: Mother Sheep
npcs.greeting: Baa! Oh, a kind face at last.

locals.name: Beachcomber Nell
lines: Every tide brings something new. Yesterday, a boot.
Today, the other boot!
Old Shelly says the Mud Eagles snatch all the pretty shells.
I found a bottle with a message once. It said 'Hello'. So I wrote back.

locals.name: Captain Salt
lines: Forty years at sea, and I never saw a pineapple swim.
Then I came here. They don't swim. They hop.
Some say a ship sank off this shore, full of gold.
I say it was full of pineapples. Look around you.

npcs.name: Old Shelly
npcs.greeting: Click-clack! Mind the tide pools, youngster.

locals.name: Wil
lines: I'm not lost. I'm exploring.
...Okay, I'm a little lost.
Did my sister send you? Tess worries too much.
The wisps keep showing me the way out, then giggling.
Tell Tess I'll be home soon. Right after I find the way.

locals.name: Granny Thistle
lines: Glow-caps for a sleeping draught. Sparkle-ferns for a waking one.
Never mix them up. Ask Dozywick how that went.
Willow the Wisp fades a little more each night.
The Shade Puffs drink the moonlight, poor dear.

npcs.name: Willow the Wisp
npcs.greeting: Shh... the woods are listening.

locals.name: Woodcutter Bram
lines: I'd never cut a tree that smiles. Only the grumpy ones.
There's just the one grumpy one. And I'm not cutting HIM.
He swatted my hat clean off last spring.
Little Pig asked me for sticks. I told him: bricks!

locals.name: Shepherd Lark
lines: Easy, Ember. No setting the nice adventurer on fire.
Flame Sheep make the warmest wool. If you can catch them.
Prismhaven's mayor wants them kept away from the market awnings.
Ember only sets fire to things she loves. So... everything.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: Mapping the river. It keeps moving.
Rivers don't move? Tell that to this one.
Every land is a page of Liora's book, you know. I'm drawing them all.
This is page... twelve? I've lost count of the pages.

npcs.name: Little Pig
npcs.greeting: Oink! Have you seen a wolf around here?

npcs.name: Grumpy Old Oak
npcs.greeting: Hrmph. Stop smiling at me. STOP IT.

victory.title: The Forest Smiles Again
story: The Grumpy Old Oak creaks, sags, and lets out a sigh a thousand years long. Then, slowly, the corners of its bark curl up.
It will never admit it, but it rather likes the Wood Monkeys swinging in its branches. The Smiling Forest lives up to its name again.

villagerLines: The fountain sparkles at night, you know.

locals.name: Painter Ivo
lines: I'm painting Prismhaven. I've run out of colours.
There are more colours here than in my whole box.
Tilly the Toymaker wants me to paint her toys. All of them.
Have you seen the fountain at night? Every colour at once.

npcs.name: Healer Lily
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Prismhaven! Rest a while, adventurer.

npcs.name: Prismhaven Market
npcs.greeting: The finest goods this side of the rainbow!

npcs.name: Mayor Poppy
npcs.greeting: Oh! You came all the way through the Smiling Forest? Splendid!

npcs.name: Smith Iris
npcs.greeting: Monsters drop the best materials. Bring them here and we'll make something sharp.

npcs.name: Tilly the Toymaker
npcs.greeting: Oh, hello! I make a toy of every monster I've seen a card of. Found any cards on your travels?

locals.name: Granny Edda
lines: Soup for Mister Frost. Cold soup, he insists.
He's a dear, but he won't come down. Says it's too warm.
Mind the wolf on the way up. He's all teeth and manners.
There's a chest up at the top too. Nobody knows who left it.

locals.name: Dwarf Fennick
lines: Seven of us, there were. Now it's just me and six snowmen.
The others went down to Ingothold for the winter.
I stayed for the apples. Have you tried them? Not the shiny ones.
A princess kept house for us once. She's off being royal now.

npcs.name: Big Bad Wolf
npcs.greeting: Grrr… what big eyes you have. All the better to FIGHT you with!

victory.title: Nobody's Afraid Anymore
story: The Big Bad Wolf huffs, puffs and runs off into the snow with its tail between its legs. It won't be blowing any houses down.
Red hoods can walk Snow White Forest without looking over their shoulders. Mayor Poppy will want to hear, and Prismhaven is buzzing with news from Moonwhisper.

npcs.name: Mister Frost
npcs.greeting: Brrr-illiant to see you!

npcs.name: Treasure Chest
npcs.greeting: A chest, left at the top for whoever climbs this far.

locals.name: Old Reed
lines: Ribbit. Sorry. Live here long enough, it slips out.
The Frog Prince says he's a real prince. They all say that.
He lost his golden ball in the pond. The Water Slugs sit on it like eggs.
The frogs sing all night. Meadowbrook complains. I sleep like a log.

locals.name: Duck-Keeper Maud
lines: That little grey duckling? Don't you listen to the Mud Slimes.
Every swan was a duckling once. Every single one.
One day it'll fly north to Swan Lake. You'll see.

npcs.name: Frog Prince
npcs.greeting: Ribbit. I am a prince, you know. Truly.

npcs.name: Ugly Duckling
npcs.greeting: Oh... hello. You don't think I'm ugly, do you?

locals.name: Lamplighter Ansel
lines: Keep to the road, friend. The lights off it aren't mine.
I light these lanterns every night. The Great Wisp blows them out.
Travellers follow its pretty light and never come back.
Well. They come back. Very muddy and very embarrassed.

locals.name: Dwarf Tolly
lines: The cavern's ours. Was ours. The rats have it now.
A Rat King, if you please! With a crown and everything.
Ingothold is cut off till someone sorts him out.
Bring a light. And cheese. Rats love cheese.

npcs.name: Brave Mouse
npcs.greeting: Squeak! Small, but brave!

npcs.name: Great Wisp
npcs.greeting: Ooooh, follow the pretty light... just a little further... hee hee!

victory.title: The Light Goes Out
story: The Great Wisp flickers, giggles one last time and goes out like a candle. All over the valley, the little lights fade with it.
Travellers can keep to the road again; Shiverdell is only a dark valley now. Only the cavern to the east still squeaks.

npcs.name: Treasure Chest
npcs.greeting: A chest, left at the top for whoever climbs this far.

locals.name: Scout Hode
lines: Ingothold sent me to scout. I've scouted. It's rats.
Big rats. And a king rat, with a crown made of spoons.
Our spoons! From Ingothold!
Sort him out and we'll make you a new set. Of spoons.

npcs.name: Rat King
npcs.greeting: Squeak! Who dares enter MY cavern? Bow to the king!

victory.title: The Rat King Falls
story: The Rat King's crown rolls across the cavern floor and spins to a stop. The rats look at it, look at each other, and scatter.
With no king in the way, the dwarves of Ingothold aren't cut off anymore. Tell Elder Oak: the road south through Shiverdell can open at last.

locals.name: Old Miner Dunmore
lines: Ingothold steel! Best in the world. Ask anyone. Ask me.
We were cut off for a year when the Rat King took the cavern.
Then someone sorted him out. Was that you? Have a nod, then.
Crystal Mountain's south of here. Gem Crawlers. Good shells.

npcs.name: Healer Brunhild
npcs.greeting: Hammer-bruised? Sit down, I'll patch you up.

npcs.name: Dwarven Forge
npcs.greeting: Forged in Ingothold, built to last a thousand years!

npcs.name: Chief Brom
npcs.greeting: You cleared the cavern? Then Ingothold owes you one, friend.

npcs.name: Smith Ingot
npcs.greeting: Ingothold steel is the finest there is. Show me what you've gathered.

locals.name: Caravan Master Zara
lines: The caravans wait. There's a dragon in the oasis.
A drunk dragon. Singing. Badly.
We used to rest there. Now we rest here and complain.
Sober him up and the first figs are yours.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: The sand moves every night. My map of here is mostly guesses.
I drew a dune. By morning it was a different dune.
Somewhere out here, a lamp holds a genie. Or a very cramped lizard.
This page of Liora's book is the hardest to draw.

npcs.name: Drunk Dragon
npcs.greeting: *hic* Heyyy… you wanna piece of this? *hic*

victory.title: A Dragon Sobers Up
story: The Drunk Dragon hiccups out one last puff of smoke, lies down by the oasis and starts to snore. It's going to wake up with a terrible headache.
The caravans can come back to the oasis, and Ingothold's trade with them. Chief Brom will want to hear, and with the desert safe, the roads out of Ingothold can open.

npcs.name: Puss in Boots
npcs.greeting: Good day! A fine pair of boots you have.

locals.name: Miner Greta
lines: Gem Crawlers carry the best crystal on their backs.
Ingothold's forge wants every shell they shed.
Pebble up the hill was just a boulder in my grandad's day. Then he woke up.
The tallest peak glitters at sunrise. Something's up there.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: Made it! The view from this page is the best in the book.
I can see Ingothold's chimneys from here.
Somebody left that chest. Not me. I only leave footprints.
Getting down is the part I never plan for.

npcs.name: Pebble
npcs.greeting: ...rumble. Oh! Sorry, I was napping.

npcs.name: Treasure Chest
npcs.greeting: A chest, left at the top for whoever climbs this far.

locals.name: Mochi Maker Hana
lines: Moon-mochi, fresh pounded! Well. Ordinary mochi.
The Queen's mochi went missing. Everyone looks at me.
I didn't take it! I only make it. Very different.
Between us... I think the Moon Rabbits ate it themselves.

locals.name: Stargazer Lune
lines: Stardust can't fly while the skeletons roam.
Out here the stars feel close enough to pocket.
I count them every night. I'm on star nine thousand and four.
Nine thousand and five. Oh, that one's moving. That's Stardust!

npcs.name: Stardust
npcs.greeting: Neigh... the stars are restless tonight.

npcs.name: Moon Rabbit Queen
npcs.greeting: Who stole my moon-mochi? Was it YOU? Hop to it and face me!

victory.title: The Queen Hops Home
story: The Moon Rabbit Queen sits down with a bump, ears drooping. Then a small rabbit peeks out from behind the throne, cheeks full, whiskers dusted with mochi.
Mystery solved. The queen scoops up the little thief and hops back up to the moon, and Moonwhisper can sleep under a quiet full moon again.

locals.name: Courier Dot
lines: Letters for Meadowbrook! Letters for Larkspur! Letters for... smudged.
The wind took three letters today. Somewhere a goose is very well informed.
Gooey Grotto? I don't deliver there. Everything comes back sticky.
If you see a letter blowing about, it's probably mine.

locals.name: Kite-Flyer Wynn
lines: This is the windiest place in Storyleaf! Perfect for kites.
I lost my red kite last week. It flew west, toward the grotto.
Something gooey and golden bounces out of there at night.
Grandma says it's the Gilded Brute, counting his treasure.

locals.name: Prospector Goldie
lines: Gold in the grotto! Real gold! ...Slimy gold.
The slimes eat coins and get shinier. I just follow them about.
Their boss calls himself the Gilded Brute. Says it's all for the Gilded King.
Never met this king. I bet he's slimy too.

npcs.name: Gilded Brute
npcs.greeting: The Gilded King's treasure is mine! Mine, mine, MINE!

victory.title: Fool's Gold
story: The Brute topples back into its hoard, and the hoard goes clink. Pebbles. Painted gold, every last one.
If the Gilded King was ever here, it left long ago. With no one to shout at them, the Golden Slimes go back to bouncing, and Elder Oak will have a good laugh.

locals.name: Gretel the Baker
lines: Don't nibble the houses, dear. Somebody might live in them.
I did, once. Long story. There was an oven.
These days I just bake. Gumdrops, mostly.
Wolves prowl the peaks at night. They don't like sugar. More for us.

locals.name: Hansel
lines: My sister says I eat too much. I'm just checking the mountain's still sugar.
It is. Mostly.
There's a chest at the very top of the peak. I hope it's full of fudge.
Mother Sheep's lambs came through here. The wolves took them west.

npcs.name: Treasure Chest
npcs.greeting: A chest, left at the top for whoever climbs this far.

locals.name: Bo-Peep
lines: I've lost my sheep, and I don't know where to find them.
Everyone says leave them alone and they'll come home.
Everyone hasn't met the Howlmaster.
If you climb up there... tell the lambs Bo-Peep is waiting at the bottom.

locals.name: Huntsman Corwin
lines: This is the Howlmaster's hill. Even the crows whisper here.
He keeps the stolen lambs at the top, where he can watch them.
I'm a huntsman. I don't fight wolves. I just keep an eye on them.
From very far away. Like now.

npcs.name: Howlmaster
npcs.greeting: Grrr... the sheep's lambs are ours. Turn back, little hero.

victory.title: The Lambs Come Home
story: The Howlmaster limps off into the dark, and the pack slinks after it. Behind a rock, something small says baa.
Mother Sheep's lambs are free, and they know the way home over Gumdrop Peaks. Nella the Tailor will be glad: no wool is finer than a happy lamb's.

villagerLines: The fountain sparkles at night, you know.

locals.name: Birdwatcher Pell
lines: Bluebirds nest on every roof in Larkspur. Bring an umbrella.
Nella the Tailor wants feathers for a dress. A swan's dress.
I told her swans don't shed for just anyone.
Swan Lake's the place. Mind the Water Slugs.

npcs.name: Healer Mei
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Larkspur. Let me see those scrapes.

npcs.name: Larkspur Market
npcs.greeting: Cloth, potions and charms, fresh from the capital!

npcs.name: Nella the Tailor
npcs.greeting: Mind the thread! Larkspur's finest tailor, at your service.

locals.name: Odette
lines: One, two, three, turn... The swans taught me that.
By day I dance. By night... well, never mind the night.
A sorcerer's spell, they say. I say it's good exercise.
Have you seen the little grey duckling? It hides from the Water Slugs.

locals.name: Boatwright Hugo
lines: This jetty gets you halfway to the island. The other half is swimming.
There's a footbridge, mind. I just prefer my way.
The swans come home in spring. They land right... about... there.
Old Swan Keeper's fed them since he was a cygnet himself.

npcs.name: Old Swan Keeper
npcs.greeting: The swans come home in spring. Every one of them was once an ugly duckling.

locals.name: Kip
lines: Shh! I'm catching a ladybug. A giant one.
They're the size of ponies here! Thumbelina rides one.
She's tiny. Thumb-tiny. Hence the name.
She wants to cross the pond to see her prince. The Lotus Sprites won't let her.

locals.name: Mister Mole
lines: I live underground, you know. Very sensible. No sun.
I asked Thumbelina to marry me. She said she'd think about it.
That was three summers ago. Still thinking, I expect.
The tunnels down there run to the Rat Cavern. Ghastly neighbours.

npcs.name: Thumbelina
npcs.greeting: Oh! Hello, giant. Please mind the lily pads, one of them is my house.

locals.name: Old Carver Beppo
lines: I carved half the puppets on this hill. Long ago.
They danced for the children at the fair. Such joy.
Then the Marionette King took up their strings, and they never stopped.
Cut his strings, friend. Set my puppets free.

locals.name: Fiddler Rook
lines: The puppets dance to my tune. Watch! ...See? Nothing.
They only dance for their king now.
I play anyway. The animals will come back when it's safe.
Hermit Orrin says they're waiting just over the hill.

npcs.name: Hermit Orrin
npcs.greeting: The puppets on the hill used to dance for children. Now they don't stop.

npcs.name: Marionette King
npcs.greeting: Dance! Dance for your king, forever and ever!

victory.title: The Strings Are Cut
story: The Marionette King's strings go slack. All over the hill the puppets stop mid-step and sit down, as if someone finally told them they could rest.
Hermit Orrin says they used to dance for children. Maybe one day they will again, but only when they want to. The animals can come home to Marionette Rise.

locals.name: Hilde the Fisher
lines: Dwarves don't fish, they say. Dwarves say a lot of things.
I caught a fish with a glowing stone in its belly once.
Ambrose said it was Dreamstone and took it off to study. I wanted it for soup.
The golems roll down to drink at dusk. Keep off the shore then.

locals.name: Scholar Wendel
lines: Ambrose sent me to count the golems. I've got as far as 'lots'.
Their cores glow like the lamps in Liora's temple.
Some say her treasure lies south, in the Hidden Steppe.
Something guards it there. Something that hits very hard.

npcs.name: Ambrose the Wise
npcs.greeting: The goddess Liora hid her treasure where only the patient look.

locals.name: Sleepwalker Mabel
lines: Zzz... five more minutes...
Zzz... the bread's in the oven... zzz...
Mmm? Is it morning? ...No? Lovely. Zzz...
Zzz... wake Rosalind... the rock... it snores... zzz...

locals.name: Watchman Ollie
lines: I'm the night watchman. I watch the night. It's very quiet.
Everyone in Dozywick's been asleep for a year. Even the cat.
Except Jory and me. Jory's too worried. I'm too... what was I saying?
The Craghulk snores in its cave. Every snore, the whole town sighs.

npcs.name: Jory
npcs.greeting: Rosalind fell asleep a year ago and never woke up. The whole town did.

npcs.name: Craghulk
npcs.greeting: Rrrrmmmbbllle... sleep... everyone... sleep...

victory.title: Dozywick Wakes Up
story: The Craghulk crumbles into a heap of quiet stones. The snoring that filled the cave for a whole year stops.
In town, someone yawns, then someone else. For the first time in a year, Rosalind's eyes open, and Jory has a whole year of news to tell.

locals.name: Herder Tamsin
lines: Steady, Brindle. It's just thunder. Probably.
Old Ox's friends wander all over the steppe now.
Four of them, tail to tail, and no lion dared come near. Now look.
If you see one, tell them the old ox misses them.

locals.name: Treasure Hunter Jasper
lines: The goddess's treasure is out here. I can smell it.
It smells like dust. Mostly dust.
There's a guardian, they say. Morvane. Hits for thousands.
I'm waiting for someone else to go first. Want to go first?

npcs.name: Morvane
npcs.greeting: The goddess's treasure has a guardian, and it is me.

victory.title: The Goddess's Treasure
story: Morvane sinks to one knee. “Then guard it well,” it rumbles, and fades into the grass like a shadow at noon.
Where it stood, Dreamstone glows in the earth, bright as a golem's heart. Ambrose the Wise will want to hear, but the ore's trail runs on, south to Sneezle Isle.

npcs.name: Old Ox
npcs.greeting: Moo... there were four of us once, and no lion dared come near.

locals.name: Ume the Picker
lines: Achoo! Sorry. Everyone sneezes here. It's the pollen.
Little Crab grew a whole persimmon tree from one seed!
Now the apes come down from the hills to raid it.
Share the harvest, Little Crab says. The apes don't share.

locals.name: Castaway Fitz
lines: Washed up here ten years ago. Achoo! Never left.
Who'd leave? Sun, persimmons, a mountain to climb.
Somebody hid a chest at the top of the peak. Achoo!
I'd fetch it myself, but... achoo! ...the pollen's worse up there.

npcs.name: Little Crab
npcs.greeting: Oh! Mind the persimmons, they fall hard around here.

npcs.name: Treasure Chest
npcs.greeting: A chest, left at the top for whoever climbs this far.

locals.name: Bridge Warden Aldric
lines: Halt! ...Sorry. Habit. Cross away.
I've watched this bridge since the Tidewater Shrine sank.
Some nights you can hear its bells under the ice.
The Temple Keeper says something still guards it down there.

locals.name: Ice Fisher Brin
lines: Fish bite better when it's cold. So do I.
I pulled up a bell once. A little silver one, all green with weed.
From the old shrine, says the Temple Keeper, who keeps it safe now.
Some nights the lake rings back.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: The island's easy to draw. Round, with a tree. Done!
The lake's harder. It freezes, then it thaws.
Briarmere's page is near the end of Liora's book.
I wonder what's on the last page. A road, I think. A green one.

npcs.name: Temple Keeper
npcs.greeting: The Tidewater Shrine sank beneath the lake long ago. Something still guards it.

locals.name: Diver Marisol
lines: I dive down to the old halls. Hold your breath and kick!
The jellies glow like lanterns down there.
In the deepest hall something big sleeps. It breathes in tides.
I don't go to the deepest hall.

locals.name: Pilgrim Sela
lines: I walk the shrine's halls every day, as my teachers did.
The water rose long ago. We kept walking.
The Wavecrest Dragon was a guardian once. Now it guards only its anger.
Be gentle with it, if you can.

npcs.name: Wavecrest Dragon
npcs.greeting: The lake keeps its secrets. So will your bones.

victory.title: The Tide Turns
story: The Wavecrest Dragon sinks into the deepest pool of the temple, and the water goes still for the first time in an age.
The Tidewater Shrine still keeps its secrets, but no longer with teeth. The Temple Keeper can walk its halls again, and boats can cross Briarmere without fear.

locals.name: Bard Lyle
lines: Hello? ...hello? ...hello?
Oh! A real person. I thought you were another echo.
The hollow whispers. Mostly about the Silver Wraith.
The Warden holds the only way through to the Emerald Road. Few get past.

npcs.name: Silverfang Warden
npcs.greeting: The Silver Wraith sends his regards.

victory.title: The Way Is Open
story: The Warden's silver armour clatters to the cave floor, empty. Whatever was inside has fled, back to the master it served.
Travellers can pass through the Whispering Hollow to the Emerald Road again. The Emerald Guard will want to hear. And somewhere far away, the Silver Wraith knows your name.

locals.name: Tin Woodman
lines: Oil can... oil can...
Ah, that's better. I've stood here rusting since the dragon came.
I'm walking to the Emerald City. For a heart.
The dragon at the gate won't let anyone by. Not even a polite tin man.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: The last page! Or nearly. The Emerald City is just past the dragon.
I've drawn every page of Liora's book. All but one.
I'll draw the city when someone clears the way.
No rush. I'm very good at waiting, and very bad at dragons.

npcs.name: Emerald Guard
npcs.greeting: Follow the road to the Emerald City. Nobody said it was safe.

npcs.name: Emerald Dragon
npcs.greeting: At the end of the road, a dragon. Of course there is.

victory.title: The Emerald Gates
story: The Emerald Dragon lowers its great head and steps aside. Behind it, the gates of the Emerald City shine green in the evening light.
From a wooden sword in Meadowbrook to the gates of the Emerald City, you've walked the longest road in Storyleaf. The Emerald Guard will hardly believe it.

npcs.name: Treasure Chest
npcs.greeting: A chest, left at the top for whoever climbs this far.
